main_text.l: tum exteriorem. Et probatur, nam quo
magis descendunt lineæ ab externo cir-
culo, magis accedunt inter se, vnde maio-
ra semper designabunt, seu relinquent
spatia in primo circulo, & minora in se-
cundo. Quare ad hoc tandem erit deuen-
iendum, vt occupparo circulo toto con-
centrico, adhuc maneant spatia in exter-
no ad linearum ductiones, vt patet in
hac figura.
Hoc autem dato, non possunt â quouis puncto
loculorum a.b. c. d. cæterisque in
peripheria manentibus duci lineæ ad centrum,
eò quòd aliquando tandem non
aderunt in circulo minori spatia vlla, per
quæ transeant sine penetratione, vt patet
in superiori parte lineis occupata. Vnde patet
non verificari axioma, quòd ab om-
ni puncto ad omne duci possit linea (nisi
mentaliter, & in abstracto) constat igi-
tur, pauciora esse puncta in minori cir-
culo, quàm in maiori: ab isto enim aliæ
possent deduci lineæ, quæ non transirent
per illum.
Objicies 4.demonstrat Euclides in omni ni

page.notes: The diagram (a circle with radiating lines and sectors lettered A, B, C, D) is described, not transcribed. The word "occupparo" and "vt patet in" with the line-end mark are printed as seen. The last line "ni" is a catchword-like fragment at the foot of the column, kept in the text. Faint marks at the bottom right are a digitiser's stamp and were left out.
